Sequential assessment 2026-09-12:
Current source confirms the unsupported type: GiftiDataType has UInt8/Int32/Float32/Other; expectedByteCount and double binary decoding lack Float64. This is an interoperability extension, not a GIFTI conformance bug: the specification lists UInt8, Int32 and Float32, as documented by NiBabel (https://nipy.org/nibabel/reference/nibabel.gifti.html). NiBabel permits additional types, so interoperability is still useful; current explicit rejection does not silently corrupt data. No actual Float64 source artifact accompanies this issue. P3 under the user's core-correctness/performance-first policy; do not make this a prerequisite for current first-level or PHRF work.

Refined acceptance:
- Document Float64 as an accepted reader extension; do not claim it is a required GIFTI data type or imply downstream adoption.
- Recognize NIFTI_TYPE_FLOAT64, validate eight-byte element counts and overflow before binary decoding, and preserve double precision end to end.
- Test public JVM/JS readers with an independent Float64 fixture (including values distinguishable from Float32), ASCII and both binary endian orders; exercise compressed input through the existing platform decompression path.
- Reject malformed/truncated payloads and unsupported integer/label conversions explicitly; inspect ASCII integer decoding as well as binary decoding so adding Float64 to the shared ASCII parser does not accidentally admit it on integer paths.
- Keep this bounded to ScalaFIM reader support. Neuropublish changing its own rejection policy is downstream work, not closure evidence here.
